subject: Re: FintechAI Post-call pricing & latency trade-offs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Meyer <alex@fintechai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: FintechAI discovery recap - token volumes, target $/1M, latency SLOs

Alex - thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary use case: conversational summaries + transaction categorization in the product UI.
- Current expected steady-state volume: ~10M tokens/month (text in/out). Growth plan: 10x over 12 months to ~100M tokens/month if POC metrics look good.
- Target budget range (initial): $5k- $25k / month while validating. Finance has said they can expand if unit economics justify.
- Unit economics target you mentioned: goal is roughly $20- $30 per 1M tokens (hard constraint for yr1).
- Latency SLO: product team prefers p95 <= 300ms for short assistant queries. They said they're willing to accept p95 up to 500ms for some batched/async workflows.

A few practical points on trade-offs (high level):
- Hosted Standard: fastest path to production, predictable per-token pricing, streaming support for low tail latency but higher unit cost. Good for early demos and user-facing low-latency flows.
- Dedicated / Reserved: lower $/1M token equivalent at commit levels (better for sustained high volume >200M tokens/mo) but requires a short procurement lead time. Lower marginal cost, more predictable latency at scale.
- Batching: aggressive batching (continuous batching) reduces $/1M but increases tail latency. We can tune max wait time to balance p95 targets.
- Streaming vs chunked: streaming helps perceived latency for long outputs (tokens delivered as generated) but doesn't always reduce compute cost; it can increase overhead if many tiny streams are used.

Proposed next steps:
1) Alex - can you confirm target monthly tokens for the first 3 months (estimates: 10M / 30M / 60M)? Also share the typical prompt+response token length distribution (samples or percentiles).
2) We'll send a short pricing comparison (hosted tiers vs equivalent dedicated economics) and a recommended config with expected $/1M token ranges and expected p95. I've attached a short unit economics summary and a pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx.
3) If you want to validate latency, we can do a 2-week pilot on Hosted Pro with streaming enabled for the critical paths.

Attaching: pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx, redwood_unit_economics_summary.pdf (quick model), SOW_template.docx (procurement starter).

Thanks - Marissa

Subject: Re: FintechAI discovery recap - pricing scenarios & latency tradeoffs

Alex / Sanjay - see requested scenarios below. I’ve kept the optics conservative; exact numbers depend on model selection (smaller opt models vs Llama2-class vs larger instruction models). Attached are the detailed sheets (pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx) and a short unit economics summary.

Scenario A - Hosted Pro (streaming enabled) - recommended for pilot (no infra commit)
- Expected per-1M token cost (approx): $28 for baseline models; $35+ for larger state-of-the-art models.
- 10M tokens/mo: list price spend ~$280 (pilot discounts available) - note: this is illustrative; final rounding + tokenization differences apply.
- p95 latency: 150-350ms (short queries) when streaming + moderate batching disabled. For longer outputs, streaming improves perceived latency.
- Notes: Good for fast time-to-value; marginal cost higher, but zero infra commitment and immediate scale.

Scenario B - Dedicated (6mo commit) - recommended when sustained >150-200M tokens/mo
- Equivalent $/1M token (amortized across committed capacity & utilization): ~$12- $18 per 1M tokens depending on commit level and utilization.
- Latency p95: consistently <200-300ms for short queries at steady load (less variability due to reserved capacity).
- Ops: Procurement lead time ~2-4 weeks. Requires basic networking/contract setup.

Batching & SLO knobs (how we tune cost vs latency):
- Continuous batching: reduces compute cost by ~20-40% at high concurrency but adds tail latency. You can set max wait window (e.g., 8-50ms) to hit a p95 target.
- Max batch size: larger batch sizes lower $/1M but increase p95.
- Streaming toggles: enable streaming on the user-facing path to keep perceived latency low while allowing background batching for non-critical calls.

Example guidance (for your target p95 <=300ms):
- For pilot (10-50M/mo): Hosted Pro with streaming + conservative batching (max wait 10-15ms) => expect p95 ~200-350ms, cost ~$25-35 / 1M.
- If finance requires ~$20 / 1M and you expect growth to >100M/mo within 6-12mo, plan for a Dedicated conversion at that milestone; we can model a stepped commit (3mo monitor -> 6/12mo commit).

Recommended next steps:
1) You: share sample token distribution (percentiles) and a short list of 10 representative requests/responses.
2) We: run a 2-week pilot on Hosted Pro, streaming enabled for primary flows; we’ll collect p95 and cost metrics and produce a conversion plan.
3) Sanjay: I’ve attached the SOW_template.docx - if procurement wants a draft SOW we can fill it and route for signature once pilot and pricing are approved.

If you want, I can put numbers into the HubSpot deal and a 1-pager comparison for procurement. Happy to jump on a 30m session this week to walk through the trade-offs.

Thanks - Marissa
